Teams meet two to four times yearly in person, in interesting locations around the world, to align on strategy and execution.</p> <p>The company is founder led, profitable and growing. Canonical has been a remote-first company since its inception in 2004.​ Working here is a step into the future, and will challenge you to think differently, work smarter, learn new skills, and raise your game.</p> <h3>Canonical is an equal opportunity employer</h3> <p>We are proud to foster a workplace free from discrimination. Diversity of experience, perspectives, and background create a better work environment and better products. <a href="https://canonical.com/careers/diversity/identity">Whatever your identity, we will give your application fair consideration.</a></p>

title: Staff Software Engineer, Security Foundations
description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.</p> <p>The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OuZIb5zszQI">Co-create the future with us</a> as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.</p> <p>*<em>Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h1><strong style="font-size: 14px;">An overview of this role</strong></h1> <p>As a Staff Software Engineer, you'll help lead two important areas for GitLab Security: the data layer behind our vulnerability and dependency management capabilities, and our move toward services outside the GitLab monolith. You'll design and develop systems that ingest, store, index, and query security report data, including integrations with key third-party systems. With a strong focus on PostgreSQL and scalable backend design, your work will support security features delivered by teams across GitLab.</p> <p>You'll take ownership of large deliverables from early ideas through implementation, working directly with product, design, frontend, and engineering partners to shape the technical and product roadmap. You'll stay hands-on across GitLab's Ruby on Rails application and newer services, including greenfield projects, while helping the team build its expertise in modular service design.</p> <p><strong>What you’ll do</strong></p> <ul> <li>Lead large technical deliverables from initial problem definition through delivery, often across multiple months or quarters.</li> <li>Design and develop backend systems for vulnerability and dependency management, including security report ingestion, storage, indexing, querying, and integrations with key third-party systems.</li> <li>Build and improve systems using Ruby on Rails and PostgreSQL, and contribute to newer services using technologies such as Go or Rust where appropriate.</li> <li>Shape technical plans, break down complex work, and help other engineers deliver effectively.</li> <li>Work directly with product, design, frontend, and engineering partners to make clear decisions, resolve constraints, and deliver measurable progress.</li> <li>Influence the team's product and technical roadmap through hands-on investigation, clear proposals, and iterative delivery that demonstrates progress in each monthly release cycle.</li> <li>Apply a security mindset when designing systems, including considering how GitLab identifies and handles malicious or vulnerable software packages.</li> <li>Define patterns for modular services, provide technical leadership when vulnerability management work spans multiple GitLab areas, and share that expertise across GitLab Security.</li> <li><span data-sheets-root="1">Take part in on-call or operational support where your team’s ownership model requires it.</span></li> </ul> <p><strong>What you’ll bring</strong></p> <ul> <li>Experience leading complex backend projects from idea through delivery while remaining hands-on with design and development.</li> <li>Strong PostgreSQL experience, including evidence of query optimization, table optimization, and write-ahead log management in data-intensive systems.</li> <li>Strong professional experience with Ruby on Rails or  Go and comfort working in Ruby on Rails day to day. Experience with large monoliths is helpful, along with an interest in working across languages and services.</li> <li>Experience shaping delivery plans, guiding technical decisions, and supporting the work of other engineers.</li> <li>The ability to collaborate with a range of partners and explain technical trade-offs clearly.</li> <li>Experience communicating with leaders, leading peers through complex delivery, identifying constraints, and moving work forward.</li> <li>Experience using security tooling for activities such as vulnerability triage and remediation, or professional experience building vulnerability management, dependency management, or related security products.</li> <li>Experience with large-scale data systems or established software products. We welcome transferable experience from outside the security domain.</li> <li>Fluency in using artificial intelligence tools to improve delivery while applying sound engineering judgment.</li> </ul> <p> </p> <p><strong>About the team</strong></p> <p>The Vulnerability Management team contributes to GitLab's move toward modular services and will help other Security teams adopt these patterns over time. Today, we include two Staff Software Engineers, two Senior Software Engineers, and one Intermediate Software Engineer across the United Kingdom, Poland, the Netherlands, and India. You'll work closely with us, product partners, and engineering leaders across GitLab.</p> <p>We work with clear goals and shared priorities. You'll receive clear context and outcomes, then have the space to own delivery, communicate decisions and progress, ask for help early, and work directly with the partners needed to get the job done.</p><div class="content-conclusion"><h4><strong>How GitLab Supports Full-Time Employees</strong></h4> <ul> <li><a href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/total-rewards/benefits/general-and-entity-benefits/">Benefits to support your health, finances, and well-being</a></li> <li><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/people-group/time-off-and-absence/time-off-types/#flexible-paid-time-off-pto">Flexible Paid Time Off </a></li> <li><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/company/culture/inclusion/tmrg-tmag/">Team Member Resource Groups</a></li> <li><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/total-rewards/stock-options/">Equity Compensation & Employee Stock Purchase Plan</a></li> <li><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/people-group/learning-and-development/growth-and-development/">Growth and Development Fund</a></li> <li><a href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/total-rewards/benefits/general-and-entity-benefits/#parental-leave">Parental Leave</a> </li> </ul> <p>Please note that we welcome interest from candidates with varying levels of experience; many successful candidates do not meet every single requirement. Additionally, studies have shown that people from <a href="https://about.gitlab.com/company/culture/inclusion/#examples-of-select-underrepresented-groups">underrepresented groups</a> are less likely to apply to a job unless they meet every single qualification. If you're excited about this role, please apply and allow our recruiters to assess your application.</p> <hr> <p><strong>Country Hiring Guidelines: </strong>GitLab hires new team members in countries around the world. All of our roles are remote, however some roles may carry specific location-based eligibility requirements. Our Talent Acquisition team can help answer any questions about location after starting the recruiting process.  </p> <p><strong>Privacy Policy: </strong>Please review our <a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/hiring/candidate-faq/recruitment-privacy-policy/" target="_blank">Recruitment Privacy Policy.</a> Your privacy is important to us.</p> <p>GitLab is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace and is an affirmative action employer. GitLab’s policies and practices relating to recruitment, employment, career development and advancement, promotion, and retirement are based solely on merit, regardless of race, color, religion, ancestry, sex (including pregnancy, lactation, sexual orientation, gender identity, or gender expression), national origin, age, citizenship, marital status, mental or physical disability, genetic information (including family medical history), discharge status from the military, protected veteran status (which includes disabled veterans, recently separated veterans, active duty wartime or campaign badge veterans, and Armed Forces service medal veterans), or any other basis protected by law. GitLab will not tolerate discrimination or harassment based on any of these characteristics. See also <a href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/people-policies/inc-usa/#equal-employment-opportunity-policy" target="_blank">GitLab’s EEO Policy</a> and <a href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/labor-and-employment-notices/#eeoc-us-equal-employment-opportunity-commission-notices" target="_blank">EEO is the Law</a>. If you have a disability or special need that requires <a href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/people-policies/inc-usa/#reasonable-accommodation" target="_blank">accommodation</a>, please let us know during the <a href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/hiring/interviewing/#adjustments-to-our-interview-process" target="_blank">recruiting process</a>.</p></div>

We also accept identity from enterprise identity providers through Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML) and Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP). Behind that sit more than ten token types and several session methods that grew inside the Ruby on Rails monolith. You'll help us move this work onto GATE, GitLab's new authentication and authorization platform. GATE exchanges external credentials for short-lived tokens at the edge through a Secure Token Service written in Go.You'll set our technical direction, lead the hardest protocol and migration work yourself, and help senior engineers own the rest.</p> <p>Our projects include:</p> <ul> <li value="1"><strong><strong class="textBold">OAuth across Cells:</strong></strong> Making OAuth clients, grants, and tokens work when users and organizations live in different cells</li> <li value="2"><strong><strong class="textBold">Global identities:</strong></strong> One user identity that works across organizations and cells</li> <li value="3"><strong><strong class="textBold">Token consolidation:</strong></strong> Reducing the number of token types and moving token issuance and validation out of the monolith</li> <li value="4"><strong><strong class="textBold">Identity for artificial intelligence (AI) agents and workloads:</strong></strong> OAuth for Model Context Protocol (MCP) clients, workload identity federation, and service identities with narrow scopes</li> </ul> <h2>What you'll do</h2> <ul> <li value="1">Own the technical direction for authentication protocols at GitLab, including OAuth 2.0, OIDC, SAML, and token exchange, across the Rails monolith and GATE services.</li> <li value="2">Write and drive design documents and architecture decision records (ADRs) for multi-quarter work, then break that work into increments that ship behind feature flags.</li> <li value="3">Lead migrations that must not break existing customers: token formats, client and grant state, and session behavior on GitLab.com, Self-Managed, and Dedicated.</li> <li value="4">Be hands-on in the most complex parts of the code, in Ruby on Rails and Go, and review the designs and merge requests of other engineers.</li> <li value="5">Agree interface contracts with the GATE Core, GATE Infra, Authorization, and Tenant Scale (Cells and Organizations) teams, and keep them current as the architecture changes.</li> <li value="6">Treat authentication as a security and availability boundary: threat-model new flows, add rate limits and abuse controls, and lead the technical response to authentication incidents.</li> <li value="7">Mentor senior and intermediate engineers on the team and raise the protocol and security knowledge of the whole group.</li> <li value="8">Work asynchronously with engineers in India, Europe, and the Americas, with most decisions made in writing.</li> <li><span data-sheets-root="1">Take part in on-call or operational support where your team’s ownership model requires it.</span></li> </ul> <h2>What you'll bring</h2> <ul> <li value="1">Significant experience building and running production authentication or identity systems at scale, with technical leadership across teams that moves unclear problems to written decisions and shipped code.</li> <li value="2">Deep, hands-on knowledge of OAuth 2.0 and OIDC: authorization code with Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE), refresh token rotation, token exchange, client registration, scopes, and JSON Web Tokens (JWTs) with signing keys and key rotation.</li> <li value="3">Working knowledge of SAML 2.0 single sign-on and enterprise identity integration (LDAP, System for Cross-domain Identity Management (SCIM), or similar).</li> <li value="4">Strong production experience in Ruby on Rails or Go, willingness to work in both, and experience with careful refactors, feature-flagged rollouts, and backward-compatible migrations in large, long-lived codebases.</li> <li value="5">A security mindset. You think about token theft, replay, revocation, and blast radius before you think about elegance.</li> <li value="6">Experience with multi-tenant software as a service (SaaS) systems, including data isolation and performance under high request volume.</li> <li value="7">Clear, concise written English and comfort working in an all-remote, asynchronous company.</li> <li value="8">Optional experience: authentication libraries (Doorkeeper, Devise, or OmniAuth), passkeys or multi-factor authentication, workload identity, gateways or policy engines, AI agent authentication, or multi-region architectures. Contributions to identity standards or open source identity projects are also welcome.</li> </ul> <h2>About the team</h2> <p>The Authentication group is part of the Security Platform stage, alongside Authorization, GATE Core, GATE Infra, Secrets Manager, and other security teams. We own sign-in, single sign-on, OAuth, and personal and service tokens. Our work touches every GitLab customer, and much of it is on the critical path for Cells and for GitLab's AI agent platform.</p> <p> </p> <h2> </h2><div class="content-conclusion"><h4><strong>How GitLab Supports Full-Time Employees</strong></h4> <ul> <li><a href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/total-rewards/benefits/general-and-entity-benefits/">Benefits to support your health, finances, and well-being</a></li> <li><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/people-group/time-off-and-absence/time-off-types/#flexible-paid-time-off-pto">Flexible Paid Time Off </a></li> <li><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/company/culture/inclusion/tmrg-tmag/">Team Member Resource Groups</a></li> <li><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/total-rewards/stock-options/">Equity Compensation & Employee Stock Purchase Plan</a></li> <li><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/people-group/learning-and-development/growth-and-development/">Growth and Development Fund</a></li> <li><a href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/total-rewards/benefits/general-and-entity-benefits/#parental-leave">Parental Leave</a> </li> </ul> <p>Please note that we welcome interest from candidates with varying levels of experience; many successful candidates do not meet every single requirement. title: Data Center Operations Engineer
description: <div class="content-intro"><h3>About Us</h3> <p>At Cloudflare, we are on a mission to help build a better Internet. Today the company runs one of the world’s largest networks that powers millions of websites and other Internet properties for customers ranging from individual bloggers to SMBs to Fortune 500 companies. Cloudflare protects and accelerates any Internet application online without adding hardware, installing software, or changing a line of code. Internet properties powered by Cloudflare all have web traffic routed through its intelligent global network, which gets smarter with every request. As a result, they see significant improvement in performance and a decrease in spam and other attacks. Cloudflare was named to Entrepreneur Magazine’s Top Company Cultures list and ranked among the World’s Most Innovative Companies by Fast Company.</p> <p>At Cloudflare, we’re not looking for people who wait for a polished roadmap; we’re looking for the builders who see the cracks in the Internet that everyone else has simply learned to live with. We value candidates who have the instinct to spot a "normalized" problem and the AI-native curiosity to create a solution using the latest tools. Our culture is built on iteration, leveraging AI to ship faster today to make it better tomorrow, while ensuring that every improvement, no matter how small, is shared across the team to lift everyone up. If you’re the type of person who values curiosity over bureaucracy, and that AI is a partner in solving tough problems to keep the Internet moving forward, you’ll fit right in.</p></div><p><strong>Available Locations: Boston, MA | Dallas, TX | Salt Lake City, UT  (This role requires you to be onsite 5 days a week in one of our locations)</strong></p> <h1>About the Department</h1> <p>Infrastructure Operations builds and manages the data center infrastructure behind Cloudflare's global network. The organization brings together engineering, operations, hardware and logistics teams that plan, deploy, operate and maintain our footprint in hundreds of cities worldwide. In this role, you'll help extend that footprint with a new generation of data center sites across the United States.</p> <h1>About the Role</h1> <p>We're looking for Data Center Engineers to be the hands, eyes and judgment on the ground at our new sites. You'll work on-site every day at your home data center, helping bring it online and keeping its hardware healthy once it's in production.</p> <p>You'll rack, cable and replace equipment, troubleshoot servers and network gear well past a simple parts swap, and keep every asset accurately documented from the moment it arrives. You'll work alongside colocation staff, integrators and partner teams, and support other sites remotely when the team needs you. Experienced engineers will have room to act as the technical lead for their site, mentor others, and help set the standards the team uses everywhere.</p> <p>We're building these sites to run with less manual effort than traditional data centers. When something breaks, we expect you to fix it for good, not just for today, and to use AI and automation to make the fix stick, whether that means a better runbook, a script, or a change to how the team works.</p> <p>This role is hands-on at the physical layer: hardware, cabling, and Layer 1/Layer 2 connectivity. You'll use the command line to troubleshoot servers and Layer 2 network issues, but network configuration and server provisioning are owned by partner engineering teams.</p> <h1>What You'll Do</h1> <h2>Site Builds</h2> <ul> <li>Support integrated site builds: receive and inspect hardware, rack and stack equipment, and run and dress structured cabling to standard.</li> <li>Verify integrator and contractor work against build specifications, drive defects to resolution, and make sure sites are production-ready before handoff.</li> </ul> <h2>Break/Fix and Troubleshooting</h2> <ul> <li>Triage and troubleshoot server hardware using BMC/IPMI, hardware logs, diagnostics and firmware tools. Find the root cause instead of swapping parts until something works.</li> <li>Replace components and whole systems, including servers, switches and optics, safely and with minimal disruption.</li> <li>Troubleshoot Layer 1 and Layer 2 issues: console into network devices, read interface and link state from the command line, inspect and clean optics, check light levels, and test fiber with a light meter or OTDR.</li> </ul> <h2>On-Call and Incidents</h2> <ul> <li>Take part in an on-call rotation and respond on site to incidents affecting hardware at your data center.</li> <li>Document what happened and what you did, and contribute to root-cause analysis and follow-up actions.</li> </ul> <h2>AI, Automation and Continuous Improvement</h2> <ul> <li>Solve problems for good. When an issue repeats, find the underlying cause and change the process, runbook or tooling so it doesn't come back.</li> <li>Use AI tools as part of your daily work: to speed up troubleshooting, interpret hardware and network logs, draft and improve documentation and runbooks, and summarize incidents.</li> <li>Find repetitive manual work and remove it with scripting, automation or AI-assisted workflows, or turn it into clear requirements for tooling teams.</li> <li>Share what works so the rest of the team can adopt it across every site.</li> </ul> <h2>Documentation and DCIM</h2> <ul> <li>Keep DCIM records accurate in real time, including rack elevations, cabling, power and asset location, from receipt through decommissioning.</li> <li>Follow and improve runbooks and build standards so work is repeatable across sites.</li> </ul> <h2>Logistics and Hardware Lifecycle</h2> <ul> <li>Own receiving, shipping and spares inventory at your site, and process RMAs end to end.</li> <li>Perform on-site decommissioning: unracking, serial number verification and chain of custody through handoff for secure destruction.</li> </ul> <h2>Vendors, Partners and Compliance</h2> <ul> <li>Escort and supervise colocation remote-hands staff, contractors and integrators working at your site, and hold them to our quality and safety standards.</li> <li>Work directly with partner teams to coordinate access, maintenance and escalations for your site.</li> <li>Follow physical security, access control and compliance procedures without exception, and help produce accurate evidence for audits.</li> </ul> <h2>Supporting Other Sites</h2> <ul> <li>Support other sites remotely, for example by guiding remote hands or reviewing documentation, and travel occasionally to help with builds or surges.</li> </ul> <h1>Who You Are</h1> <p><strong>Careful and precise.</strong> Clean cabling, correct labels and accurate records matter to you. If it isn't documented, it isn't done.</p> <p><strong>Dependable on your own.</strong> You're often the only Cloudflare person on site. You work independently, communicate clearly with a remote team, and know when to escalate.</p> <p><strong>Security-minded.</strong> You understand that access rules and chain of custody exist for a reason, and you follow them every time.</p> <p><strong>A troubleshooter, not a parts swapper.</strong> You want to know why something failed, and you use logs, diagnostics and the command line to find out.</p> <p><strong>Someone who makes the team better.</strong> You share what you learn, help newer teammates get up to speed, and take ownership of your site's outcomes.</p> <p><strong>AI-fluent and automation-first.</strong> Your first instinct is to solve a problem for good, not work around it again. You reach for AI tools and automation to troubleshoot faster, document better and improve how the team works, and you check the output before you trust it.</p> <h1>Required Experience</h1> <ul> <li>Hands-on experience in data center, network or server hardware operations, including working independently on site.</li> <li>Experience racking, stacking and cabling servers and network equipment, and replacing whole systems and components.</li> <li>Solid working knowledge of structured cabling standards, fiber and copper, and optics.</li> <li>Hardware troubleshooting beyond parts swaps, including BMC/IPMI, hardware logs, diagnostics and firmware.</li> <li>Comfort with the Linux command line and with network device CLIs to troubleshoot Layer 1 and Layer 2 issues.</li> <li>Experience with fiber inspection, cleaning and testing, including light meters or OTDR.</li> <li>Regular, hands-on use of AI tools in your technical work, such as troubleshooting, log analysis or documentation, and examples of improving a process instead of repeating a workaround.</li> <li>Experience with asset tracking, DCIM or inventory systems, and with receiving, shipping and RMA processes.</li> <li>Experience working in colocation facilities and with third-party vendors or contractors.</li> <li>Willingness to take part in an on-call rotation and respond on site.</li> <li>Clear written and verbal communication, including documenting work and updating tickets.</li> <li>A valid driver's license, reliable transportation, and proximity to your assigned data center.</li> <li>Ability to travel occasionally to other sites.</li> </ul> <h1>Preferred Qualifications</h1> <ul> <li>Experience as a technical lead or primary on-site contact for a data center, including leading on-site incident response.</li> <li>Experience mentoring or training other technicians or engineers.</li> <li>Experience writing runbooks, build standards or checklists used across multiple sites.</li> <li>Experience supporting or leading new data center builds or integrated rack deployments.</li> <li>Scripting experience (for example Bash or Python), or experience building automation or AI-assisted workflows that reduced manual work.</li> <li>Certifications such as CompTIA A+, Network+ or Linux+, CCNA, BICSI, or data center certifications (for example CDCP or CDCTP).</li> <li>Experience with DCIM and source-of-truth tooling such as NetBox or Nlyte, and Jira-based workflows.</li> <li>Experience at a hyperscaler, cloud provider, major CDN or similarly large infrastructure operator.</li> <li>Experience with ITAD and secure destruction processes.</li> </ul> <p>We also consider candidates earlier in their careers who bring strong fundamentals and a drive to learn.</p> <h1>Physical Requirements</h1> <ul> <li>Lift and move equipment up to 50 lbs, and handle heavier equipment with a team or lift assist.</li> <li>Stand, walk, bend, kneel and work in tight or elevated spaces for extended periods.</li> <li>Work in loud, cold, and tightly controlled data center environments.</li> <li>Use ladders, lifts and carts safely.</li> </ul> <p><em>These are essential functions of the role. Reasonable accommodations are available for qualified individuals with disabilities.</em></p

title: Dev Experiences and Community Lead (SF)
description: ABOUT SUPABASE Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth. ABOUT THE ROLE Supabase is looking for a Dev Experiences and Community Lead (SF) to help grow and scale our developer community initiatives and industry event programs. You’ll work closely with the Head of Global Events and Field Marketing to build programs that connect Supabase with developers and the broader ecosystem. This includes initiatives such as meetups, workshops, hackathons, and community activations that bring Supabase into the spaces where developers learn, build, and collaborate. As an early member of the events team, you’ll help shape how Supabase shows up in person around the world while building the playbooks and frameworks that allow these programs to scale globally. This role sits within Field Marketing and works cross-functionally across Marketing, DevRel, Partnerships, Sales and Design to support programs that deepen developer engagement, strengthen ecosystem relationships. You will also support programming around Supabase Select, our flagship user conference, including partner and community programming connected to the event. We’re a lean, remote-first team, so this role requires someone who is comfortable operating independently, experimenting with new ideas, and helping build the systems that will power Supabase’s events program as it grows. WHAT YOU’LL DO Own and Scale Community Programs - Scale Supabase developer meetups, workshops, and hackathons globally - Partner with DevRel to align community events with product launches and developer education initiatives - Coordinate community meetups around major industry events and Launch Week - Support community programming connected to Supabase Select - Support the SupaSquad advocate network through community activations Support Industry Event Activations - Support Supabase’s presence at conferences such as AWS re:Invent, KubeCon, Stripe Sessions, Dash, and other events - Coordinate developer-focused side events, meetups, and partner activations around major conferences - Collaborate with Partnerships on co-hosted events Turn Experiments Into Scalable Programs - Build playbooks and frameworks for community and ecosystem programs - Identify opportunities to scale successful initiatives across regions - Standardizing event formats and processes as program grow Collaborate Across the Events Team - Partner with the events team on logistics and execution for community programs - Support promotion and event readiness with Marketing - Help ensure strong attendee experiences and post-event follow-up WHO YOU ARE - 5–7+ years in field marketing, developer marketing, community programs or partner marketing - Experience working with developer communities or technical audiences - Strong project management and organizational skills - Comfortable collaborating cross-functionally - Curious about developer ecosystems and the communities around modern infrastructure - Able to manage multiple initiatives in a fast-moving environment Comfortable working remotely and independently - Willing to travel for events as needed NICE TO HAVE - Experience supporting developer meetups, hackathons, or workshops - Experience with community-led growth or developer advocacy programs - Experience running ecosystem or partner-led event programs WHAT WE OFFER - Fully Remote We hire globally. We believe you can do your best work from anywhere. There are no Supabase offices, but we provide a WeWork membership or co-working allowance you can use anywhere in the world. - ESOP Every team member receives ESOP (equity ownership) in the company. We want everyone to share in the upside of what we’re building together. - Tech Allowance Use this budget to set up your ideal work environment—laptop, monitor, headphones, or whatever helps you do your best work. - Health Benefits Supabase covers 100% of health insurance for employees and 80% for dependents, wherever you are. Your wellbeing and your family’s health are important to us. - Annual Off-Sites Once a year, the entire company gathers in a new city for a week of connection, collaboration, and fun. It’s a highlight of our year. - Flexible Work We operate asynchronously and trust you to manage your own time. You know what needs to be done and when. - Professional Development Every team member receives an annual education allowance to spend on learning—courses, books, conferences, or anything that supports your growth. ABOUT THE TEAM Supabase was born-remote and open-source-first. We believe our globally distributed team is our secret weapon in building tools developers love. - ~400 team members - 60+ countries - 20+ languages spoken - Over $1B raised (including our $500M Series F) - 540,000+ community members We move fast, build in public, and use what we ship. If it’s in your project, we probably use it in ours too. We believe deeply in the open-source ecosystem and strive to support—not replace—existing tools and communities.

Texas, ULS, LCTCS, OK State & U of OK</strong>.</li> <li>Expertly bridge the gap between centralized IT governance, decentralized municipal departments (e.g., public safety, transportation), and individual academic colleges to build consensus and drive enterprise platform sales.</li> </ul> <h3><strong>Precision Forecasting & Public Fiscal Cycle Mastery</strong></h3> <ul> <li>Operates with unmatched accuracy in forecasting, proactively shaping and managing a strategic pipeline aligned with municipal fiscal years, university funding cycles, and regional budget approval timelines.</li> sectors.</li> </ul> <h3><strong>Digital Transformation & Critical Infrastructure Protection</strong></h3> <ul> <li>Exhibit mastery in understanding the intricate nuances of digital transformation in <li>Identify regional market shifts, regulatory compliance mandates, and public sector-specific needs to construct pioneering digital innovation partnerships between Cloudflare and TOLA’s leading institutions.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>Examples of Desirable Skills, Knowledge, and Experience</strong></h2> <ul> <li><strong>12+ years of unparalleled experience</strong> selling complex, major local government and university ecosystems.</li> <li><strong>Deep Texas territory expertise</strong>, with a strong, active network of existing relationships across Texas county/city IT leadership, major municipal agencies, administrators, and prominent universities across the TOLA region.</li> <li><strong>Strong familiarity with public procurement protocols</strong>, including direct experience leveraging regional cooperative contracts (<strong>OMNIA, Sourcewell</strong>), <strong>DIR</strong> network resources, municipal RFP processes, and collaborative purchasing specifically <strong>CJIS, FERPA, FEDRamp, and the Higher Education Cloud Vendor Assessment Tool (HECVAT)</strong>.</li> <li><strong>Proven success in engaging and influencing</strong> at the highest Today the company runs one of the world’s largest networks that powers millions of websites and other Internet properties for customers ranging from individual bloggers to SMBs to Fortune 500 companies. Cloudflare protects and accelerates any Internet application online without adding hardware, installing software, or changing a line of code. Internet properties powered by Cloudflare all have web traffic routed through its intelligent global network, which gets smarter with every request. As a result, they see significant improvement in performance and a decrease in spam and other attacks. Advise on best practices.</li> </ul> Desirable Skills, Knowledge, and Experience<br> <ul> <li>Previous experience as a Solutions Engineer or other customer-facing technical role, ideally selling to or working with developer-led, cloud-native, or startup organizations.</li> <li>A genuine "builder" mindset and the personality to match: you enjoy talking to developers, you're curious, and you naturally gravitate toward technical problem-solving conversations.</li> <li>The ability to speak engineers' language credibly — you can hold your own on architecture, APIs, and platform design — <strong>without</strong> this being a hands-on, code-every-day developer role.</li> <li>Strong technical discovery instincts: you know how to draw out requirements, qualify fit early, and separate real needs from noise.</li> <li>A good mix of pre-sales / technical sales experience and comfort operating in an agile, fast-moving environment (joining Slack channels, iterating quickly, engaging in early-stage calls, and qualifying deals from the start).</li> <li>Solid communication, written and presentation skills, with the range to talk to both a hands-on developer and a CTO in the same day.</li> <li>Ability to work on several projects and activities concurrently.</li> <li>Highly driven, curious, team-oriented, and able to work with a sense of urgency.</li> <li>You've built web applications before, or contributed to existing web applications in a meaningful way — enough to have real empathy for how developers work.</li> <li>Polished communication and executive presentation skills with the ability to drive a discussion with a broad range of stakeholders (from the web developer to the CTO/CISO).</li> <li>Relationship building: a proven track record of building deep technical relationships with engineers and technical founders. Experience managing various stakeholder relationships to build consensus on technical solutions/projects.</li> <li>Experience managing technical sales within accounts, including developing champion-style relationships, driving technical wins, and assisting with technical validation.</li> <li>Bachelor's Degree or equivalent in relevant work experience.</li> <li>The role requires up to 50% travel to attend meetings with prospects or customers, attend conferences and other industry events, and to collaborate with your Cloudflare teammates.</li> </ul> A deep understanding of the Cloudflare Developer Platform and core industry components (and a desire to learn more):<br> <ul> <li><strong>The Cloudflare Developer Platform</strong> — serverless compute and application development with Workers, Durable Objects, Workers AI, R2, KV, D1, Vectorize, Queues, and Pages. Reminder: this is not a strict requirement at all. Candidates from all walks of life are welcome.</li> <li>You can translate technical concepts and jargon for a wide variety of audiences: from systems engineers, to front-end developers, through to technical founders and C-levels.</li> <li>You want to be constantly learning new things and teaching what you've learned to the broader team through internal and external blog posts, team demos, and product training sessions.</li> <li>You have a knack for understanding problems and finding creative ways to solve them. In an acceleratingly dangerous world, the scope of that mission has changed. We are becoming something more: critical infrastructure. Banks run their payment rails on us. Governments run public services on us. Media companies depend on us during live events. Health systems depend on us to provide care. Reliability for these customers is no longer a feature of our product. It is a mission.</p> <p>Serving that customer base demands a different operating model. Traditional support organizations route tickets. Traditional engineering organizations ship features. Neither alone is enough when the stakes are this high. We are pivoting to something different: a customer-facing engineering organization, directly engaged with our customers at scale. This is work a central dev team cannot do from the inside of the network.</p> <p>The Customer Reliability Engineering function is the spine of that pivot. CRE is SRE applied outward, the same engineering discipline, applied to the reliability of the systems our customers run on Cloudflare. You are the engineer who owns the problems that matter most to the customers who matter most, and you contribute directly to our products and tooling, in partnership with Product Engineering, to hold that standard across the entire customer base.</p> <h3><strong>The Role</strong></h3> <p>CRE is a rapid response team and a proactive engineering team. You fix things at the edge as they come up, and you help build the product capabilities that identify customer issues before they become a crisis. Both modes are equally core.</p> <p><strong>Rapid response.</strong> When a customer issue surfaces that is high-severity, cross-layer and complex, you are the engineer who answers. You reproduce the defect, isolate the root cause across Cloudflare's infrastructure and the customer's stack, drive the fix with Product Engineering, and confirm resolution. You hold on-call for high-severity incidents as part of a global shift rotation.</p> <p><strong>Proactive engineering.</strong> When no fire is burning, you work with Product Engineering and our platform teams to build the capabilities that make the next fire cheaper or unnecessary: telemetry pipelines that correlate signals across the customer base, detectors that fire before a human notices, diagnostic tooling that scales across hundreds of customers, automation that reduces toil for Customer Support. Every incident you carry generates engineering output that reduces the cost of recurrence. The work compounds.</p> <p>Cloudflare is building CRE as an AI-native function. You will work with and help build agents and tooling that pre-diagnose incidents, surface relevant logs and configuration, and propose fixes with cited evidence. Engineers who ship AI-assisted diagnostics are the ones defining this discipline.</p> <h3><strong>What You Might Work On</strong></h3> <p><strong>Rapid response:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Own a Sev-1 incident where a large financial services customer sees asymmetric latency from a single POP. Trace it through BGP routing and origin configuration. Produce the fix upstream.</li> <li>Diagnose a recurring WebSocket disconnect that a media customer has been fighting for weeks. Isolate it to a specific interaction between WAF and their origin load balancer. Drive the fix with Product Engineering.</li> <li>Partner with a government customer's SRE team during an active DDoS event. Help them shape their Magic Transit and WAF configuration in real time.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Proactive engineering:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Build, with Product Engineering, a distributed tracing capability that correlates Cloudflare edge signals with customer origin metrics so a single query tells the story of a failing request end-to-end.</li> <li>Ship a detector for a class of WAF false positives silently degrading several customers. Get it into production before the next renewal cycle.</li> <li>Prototype an AI agent that takes a new customer case, pulls relevant logs and config, and proposes a root cause with linked evidence. Deploy it internally. Measure whether it makes engineers faster. Iterate.</li> </ul> <h3><strong>Responsibilities</strong></h3> <p><strong>Rapid incident response and root cause analysis.</strong> Own the most complex, high-severity customer issues end-to-end, from first signal through confirmed resolution. Lead deep-dive debugging across the full stack: edge, network, DNS, transport, APIs, application, customer-side configuration. Reproduce defects, validate fixes with Engineering, and confirm customer-side resolution. Produce postmortems other engineers rely on. Hold on-call for high-severity incidents as part of a global rotation that includes weekends.</p> <p><strong>Proactive reliability engineering.</strong> Analyze support and telemetry signals across the customer base to find systemic risks before they become incidents. Contribute monitoring, detection, and diagnostic capability to the core product and the engineering systems that give Customer Support early visibility into customer-affecting issues. Define customer-facing reliability metrics (error rates, resolution times, repeat-contact rates) and drive measurable improvement. Write automation that reduces mean-time-to-detect and mean-time-to-resolve.</p> <p><strong>Cross-functional partnership.</strong> Manage the technical escalation lifecycle with clear ownership and timely communication. Partner with Product Engineering to drive fixes, workarounds, and configuration changes that address underlying gaps. Represent the customer reliability perspective in engineering syncs, incident reviews, and post-mortem processes.</p> <p><strong>Technical leadership and enablement.</strong> Raise the technical floor of Customer Support through pair-debugging, structured knowledge transfer, and shared tooling. Document diagnostic procedures and resolution patterns in runbooks, internal knowledge bases, and AI skills. Share insights from customer-facing incidents to improve product documentation and operational readiness.</p> <p><strong>Product and platform depth.</strong> Maintain deep, current expertise across Cloudflare's product portfolio: edge networking, DNS, CDN, WAF, DDoS mitigation, Zero Trust, Workers, and our developer platform. Anticipate customer impact from new releases and architecture changes. Serve as a go-to subject-matter expert in one or more domains.</p> <h3><strong>Requirements</strong></h3> <ul> <li>Minimum 5 years of hands-on experience in site reliability engineering, escalation engineering, systems engineering, or a comparable deeply technical support / operations role, with at least 2 years in customer-facing environments.</li> <li>Strong foundation in networking and security:</li> <ul> <li>TCP/IP fundamentals: OSI model, IPv4/IPv6 addressing, subnetting, routing, switching.</li> <li>Core protocols: DNS, HTTP/S, TLS/SSL, SMTP, SNMP, NTP.</li> <li>Routing protocols: BGP, OSPF, including path selection and route propagation.</li> <li>Firewall concepts: stateful/stateless inspection, rule sets, NAT, ACLs.</li> <li>VPN and encryption: IPSec, SSL/TLS tunnels, GRE.</li> <li>Zero Trust architecture, network segmentation, modern security models.</li> </ul> <li>Proficiency with observability and diagnostic tooling: packet capture and analysis (Wireshark, tcpdump), log aggregation (Kibana, Elasticsearch), metrics dashboards (Grafana), distributed tracing.</li> <li>Strong scripting and automation skills (Bash, Python) with a track record of shipping tooling that improves reliability and reduces toil.</li> <li>Experience with incident management, postmortem culture, and SLO/SLI-based reliability practices.</li> <li>Excellent written and verbal communication. Able to convey complex technical information clearly to engineers, leadership, and customers.</li> <li>Comfort owning ambiguous, cross-layer problems. Composure under pressure during high-severity incidents.</li> </ul> <h3><strong>Desired Skills & Experience</strong></h3> <ul> <li>SRE, DevOps, or platform engineering experience with direct customer-facing accountability.</li> <li>Deep expertise at both L3/L4 (network infrastructure) and L7 (application protocols, DNS, HTTP, WebSocket).</li> <li>Expert-level proficiency with Linux command-line tools: curl, dig, git, traceroute, mtr, strace, ss.</li> <li>Data-at-scale analysis using SQL, PromQL, or equivalent.</li> <li>Familiarity with CI/CD pipelines, infrastructure-as-code (Terraform, Pulumi), and container orchestration (Kubernetes, Docker).</li> <li>Track record of building internal tooling or diagnostic utilities that measurably improved team efficiency.</li> <li>Demonstrated technical leadership: mentoring engineers, driving cross-team initiatives, influencing outcomes without direct authority.</li> <li>Experience applying AI/ML to production engineering or operational workflows.</li> <li>Comfort engaging directly with enterprise customer engineering teams, including on calls during incidents.</li> </ul> <h3><strong>Bonus Points</strong></h3> <ul> <li>Active Cloudflare user who understands the platform as a practitioner.</li> <li>Hands-on experience with Workers, Page

Define sequencing and milestones.</p> </td> </tr> <tr> <td> <p><strong>Cross-Functional Coordination</strong></p> </td> <td> <p>Coordinate SE, CS, and Product resources against adoption milestones. Cloudflare protects and accelerates any Internet application online without adding hardware, installing software, or changing a line of code. Internet properties powered by Cloudflare all have web traffic routed through its intelligent global network, which gets smarter with every request. As a result, they see significant improvement in performance and a decrease in spam and other attacks. Cloudflare was named to Entrepreneur Magazine’s Top Company Cultures list and ranked among the World’s Most Innovative Companies by Fast Company.</p> <p>At Cloudflare, we’re not looking for people who wait for a polished roadmap; we’re looking for the builders who see the cracks in the Internet that everyone else has simply learned to live with. We value candidates who have the instinct to spot a "normalized" problem and the AI-native curiosity to create a solution using the latest tools. Our culture is built on iteration, leveraging AI to ship faster today to make it better tomorrow, while ensuring that every improvement, no matter how small, is shared across the team to lift everyone up. If you’re the type of person who values curiosity over bureaucracy, and that AI is a partner in solving tough problems to keep the Internet moving forward, you’ll fit right in.</p></div><h4><strong>Available Location - Bengaluru, India</strong></h4> <h4><strong>About the team</strong></h4> <p>The Data Intelligence & Analytics organization builds the core data platform and internal products that power decision-making across the company. We design and operate large-scale data systems, own the company’s data lake, ingestion infrastructure, and platform tooling, and develop end-to-end applications that transform complex datasets into fast, reliable, business-critical products used daily by go-to-market, product, and engineering teams. Our work sits at the intersection of data platforms, distributed systems, and product development, giving engineers the opportunity to own meaningful problems across the stack and build systems that truly run the business.</p> <h4><strong>About the role</strong></h4> <p>We are looking for an experienced data scientist to join our Bangalore team and help scale the next generation of our AI/ML models. In this role, you will train predictive models and the workflows behind AI-driven applications, Agents, Chatbots that power teams across the company, including go-to-market, engineering, and product. Because the products we build are initiated and owned by the team, you will be involved end-to-end — from shaping requirements and designing systems to implementation, deployment, and long-term ownership.</p> <p>You will focus on building scalable, reliable AI/ML models, services and GenAI powered application backends,  partnering closely with data and full-stack engineers to deliver new features and operate the pipelines and platforms behind our products. Our stack spans multiple languages and technologies, including Python, React, and TypeScript, and continues to evolve. Many of our applications also incorporate strong AI components, giving you opportunities to work with modern AI infrastructure and tools such as vector databases, MCP-based services, and Workers AI.</p> <p><strong>What you'll do</strong></p> <ul> <li>Partner and align with business leaders, stakeholders, product managers and internal teams to understand the business and product challenges and goals and address them using predictive analytics in a globally distributed environment.</li> <li>Understand data landscape i.e tooling, tech stack, source systems etc. and work closely with the data engineering team to improve the data collection and quality.</li> <li>Understand business/product strategy and high-level roadmap and align analysis efforts to enable them with data insights and help achieve their strategic goals.</li> <li>Strong audience focused presentation and storytelling skills focused on key takeaways in a crisp and concise manner.</li> <li>Define, implement, and train statistical, machine learning, deep learning and generative AI models.</li> <li>Use software engineering best practices to publish model scores/insights/learnings at scale within the company.</li> <li>Ability to define and spot macro and micro levels trends with statistical significance on a regular basis and understand key drivers driving those trends.</li> <li>Active role in hiring, growing, and mentoring the data scientist team in Bengaluru.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Examples of desirable skills, knowledge and experience</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelors or M.S in Computer Science, Statistics, Mathematics, or other quantitative fields.</li> <li>5+ years of data scientist experience with proven industry experience in a large scale environment (PBs scale & globally distributed teams). fast-growing SaaS business based company is preferred.</li> <li>Strong experience working with business functions such as Finance, Sales, and Marketing to build models and drive impactful business outcomes (eg: customer and revenue growth)</li> <li>Strong experience in scientific computing using Python</li> <li>Experience with Spark, SQL, Tableau, Google Analytics, BigQuery (or any other Big data/Cloud equivalent) etc.</li> <li>Experience working with and processing structured, unstructured, and semi-structured data. </li> <li>Strong cross-functional collaboration experience with data engineering and data analysts teams within the function.</li> <li>Proven track record of applying data insights and machine learning in order to address business needs and drive revenue.</li> <li>Proficiency in large language models and the frameworks (Langchain, Langgraph, etc.) necessary for implementing GenAI applications, such as AI Agents, chatbots and related use cases.</li> <li>Strong communication and presentation skills catered to different audiences within the company.</li> <li>Capable of working closely with business, engineering, and product teams to ensure data initiatives are aligned with business needs.</li> <li>Experience in hiring data scientists and establishing team best practices is preferred.</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><h3>What Makes Cloudflare Special?</h3> <p><span style="font-weight: 400;">We’re not just a highly ambitious, large-scale technology company. We’re a highly ambitious, large-scale technology company with a soul. Fundamental to our mission to help build a better Internet is protecting the free and open Internet.</span></p> <p><a href="https://blog.cloudflare.com/protecting-free-expression-online/"><strong>Project Galileo</strong></a><span style="font-weight: 400;">: Since 2014, we've equipped more than 2,400 journalism and civil society organizations in 111 countries with powerful tools to defend themselves against attacks that would otherwise censor their work, technology already used by Cloudflare’s enterprise customers--at no cost.</span></p> <p><strong><a href="https://www.cloudflare.com/athenian/">Athenian Project</a></strong><span style="font-weight: 400;">: In 2017, we created the Athenian Project to ensure that state and local governments have the highest level of protection and reliability for free, so that their constituents have access to election information and voter registration. Since the project, we've provided services to more than 425 local government election websites in 33 states.</span></p> <p><a href="https://1.1.1.1/"><strong>1.1.1.1</strong></a><span style="font-weight: 400;">: We released</span><a href="https://1.1.1.1/"> <span style="font-weight: 400;">1.1.1.1</span></a><span style="font-weight: 400;"> to help fix the foundation of the Internet by building a faster, more secure and privacy-centric public DNS resolver. We will continue to abide by our</span><a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/1.1.1.1/privacy/public-dns-resolver"> privacy commitment</a><span style="font-weight: 400;"> and ensure that no user data is sold to advertisers or used to target consumers.</span></p> <p><span style="font-weight: 400;">Sound like something you’d like to be a part of? We’d love to hear from you!</span></p> <p><span style="font-weight: 400;">Please note that applicants who progress to the offer stage of the interview process may be asked to attend an in-person interview within one of the Cloudflare Offices or Cloudflare Hubs.  More details about this will be available at that stage of the interview process.</span></p> <p><span style="font-weight: 400;">This position may require access to information protected under U.S. export control laws, including the U.S. Export Administration Regulations. If you’re the type of person who values curiosity over bureaucracy, and that AI is a partner in solving tough problems to keep the Internet moving forward, you’ll fit right in.</p></div><p><strong>Available Locations: </strong></p> <ul> <li><strong>Austin, TX</strong></li> <li><strong>Atlanta, GA</strong></li> <li><strong>Denver, CO</strong></li> <li><strong>Seattle, WA</strong></li> <li><strong>Washington, DC </strong></li> </ul> <p><strong></strong></p> <p><strong>Application Deadline: December 16, 2026</strong></p> <p><strong></strong></p> <p><strong>Position Overview</strong></p> <p>Cloudflare is looking for an Automation Specialist to transform how our global Data Center Security Compliance (DCSC) team operates. This critical role is part of the Infrastructure Operations organization, which is responsible for building, scaling, and running Cloudflare's data center and network infrastructure across 700+ sites worldwide.</p> <p>The DCSC team manages physical access control and compliance auditing across one of the most complex and distributed infrastructure footprints in the industry, spanning more than 105 vendor portals, hundreds of non-portal carrier-neutral and edge partner sites, and multiple regulatory frameworks including SOC 2, ISO 27001, FedRAMP, ISMAP, and IRAP. The operational burden of this work is substantial and largely manual: user lists are pulled by hand, access control lists are reconciled by eye, evidence packages are assembled ticket by ticket, and attestation cycles consume weeks of coordinator time every quarter.</p> <p>This role exists to change that. The DCSC Automation -Specialist will design, build, and operate AI-assisted and automated workflows that eliminate the most time-consuming manual work in the DCSC operating model, freeing compliance coordinators to focus on exception handling, stakeholder relationships, and regulatory judgment rather than data gathering and reconciliation.</p> <p>This is a builder role. You will interview the team to understand each workflow, identify the highest-leverage automation targets, and ship tooling that demonstrably reduces the time it takes to close a QAR cycle, produce an audit evidence package, or manage a batch of access provisioning requests. You will work in close partnership with the DCSC coordinators, and existing automation developers, and will own the DCSC operational tooling roadmap.</p> <p><strong>Key Responsibilities</strong></p> <ol> <li><strong> Portal Automation & User List Extraction</strong></li> </ol> <ul> <li>Browser Automation: Design and maintain automated scripts (Playwright, Puppeteer, or equivalent) that log into vendor data center portals, extract user access lists, and feed structured output into the DCSC Portal and comparison pipelines replacing manual portal-by-portal data collection across 105+ portals covering 338+ sites.</li> <li>Resilience & Coverage: Build fallback handling for portals that block or rate-limit automated access; document exceptions and maintain a coverage registry tracking automation status per portal.</li> <li>Scheduled Execution: Operationalize extraction jobs on a recurring cadence aligned to QAR and MAR cycles, with alerting for failures and drift.</li> </ul> <ol> <li><strong> ACL Reconciliation & Diff Engine</strong></li> </ol> <ul> <li>Automated Comparison: Build tooling that ingests portal-extracted user lists and compares them against the master Access Control List (ACL), automatically surfacing discrepancies: users present in a portal but absent from the ACL, users on the ACL without active portal access, and role or access-level mismatches.</li> <li>Exception-Only Output: Route confirmed discrepancies directly to pre-populated Jira tickets for human review and action, eliminating the need for coordinators to perform full manual review of every user record each quarter.</li> <li>Audit Trail: Ensure all comparison runs produce immutable, timestamped records suitable for SOC 2, ISO 27001, and FedRAMP evidence requirements.</li> </ul> <ol> <li><strong> Attestation & Evidence Automation</strong></li> </ol> <ul> <li>Attestation Module: Own and extend the attestation workflow within the DCSC Portal, including automated cycle triggering, manager notification, time-stamped confirmation capture, and exception escalation, replacing manual screenshot-based evidence gathering.</li> <li>Evidence Package Builder: Build automated pipelines that compile audit-ready evidence packages for SOC 2, ISO 27001, FedRAMP, ISMAP, and IRAP control cycles, pulling attestation logs, portal extraction results, diff reports, and correspondence into structured packages keyed to specific control IDs.</li> <li>GRC Alignment: Work directly with GRC counterparts to validate that automated evidence formats meet auditor and regulatory requirements before deployment.</li> </ul> <ol> <li><strong> AI-Assisted Anomaly Detection & Triage</strong></li> </ol> <ul> <li>Access Pattern Analysis: Implement LLM-based review passes over QAR cycle output to surface patterns warranting human escalation: former employees retaining access, access creep over time, dormant accounts, and anomalous role assignments across sites.</li> <li>Ticket Intelligence: Build automation that reads incoming Jira onboarding and offboarding tickets and generates structured, portal-specific action checklists reducing coordinator cognitive load and preventing missed steps across multi-portal provisioning workflows.</li> <li>Continuous Improvement: Monitor automation output quality over time, retrain or recalibrate models as portal structures change, and maintain a feedback loop with coordinators on false positives and missed detections.</li> </ul> <ol> <li><strong> DCSC Portal Ownership & Tooling Roadmap</strong></li> </ol> <ul> <li>Platform Stewardship: Own the DCSC Portal as the operational runtime for all automation and workflow tooling ensuring it remains stable, documented, and usable by coordinators without engineering support for day-to-day tasks.</li> <li>Roadmap Management: Maintain a prioritized backlog of automation opportunities, assessed by time savings, compliance impact, and implementation complexity; present quarterly progress and priorities to DCSC leadership.</li> <li>Documentation: Produce runbooks for every automation, ensuring that no operational capability lives only in one person's head or on a local machine.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Desirable skills / Experience:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Automation Engineering: Demonstrated experience building browser automation (Playwright, Puppeteer, Selenium, or equivalent) against real-world web applications, including handling authentication flows, dynamic content, and anti-bot mitigations.</li> <li>TypeScript Proficiency: Strong skills for scripting, data wrangling, structured file I/O, and API integration. Ability to write maintainable, documented code that non-engineers can operate.</li> <li>LLM Integration: Hands-on experience integrating LLM APIs (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, or equivalent) into production workflows for classification, drafting, summarization, or anomaly detection tasks.</li> <li>Data Engineering Fundamentals: Comfort working with structured and semi-structured data at scale, diffing datasets, normalizing inconsistent formats, and producing clean outputs for downstream audit use.</li> <li>API & Workflow Integration: Experience building integrations with ticketing or ITSM systems (Jira preferred) via REST API, including automated ticket creation, status updates, and attachment handling.</li> <li>Systems Thinking: Ability to map an end-to-end manual workflow, identify the highest-leverage automation insertion points, and ship incrementally without waiting for a perfect solution.</li> <li>Workflow Archaeology: Comfortable extracting process knowledge from subject-matter experts through structured interviews turning tribal knowledge into documented, automatable workflows.</li> <li>Bias Toward Simplicity: Strong product intuition for the minimum viable automation that delivers real time savings, rather than over-engineering for edge cases.</li> <li>Compliance Awareness: Appreciation for the stakes of accuracy in a compliance context, understanding that an incorrect ACL diff or a missing evidence artifact has real audit consequences.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Soft Skills:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Communication: Able to explain automation design decisions and tradeoffs clearly to non-technical stakeholders including compliance coordinators and GRC partners.</li> <li>Ambiguity Tolerance: Vendor portals don't come with documentation. Workflows are passed down verbally. You need to be energized by figuring things out from scratch.</li> <li>Preferred Qualifications</li> <li>Experience with Cloudflare Workers or similar edge compute platforms</li> <li>Familiarity with GRC/compliance frameworks (SOC 2, FedRAMP, ISO 27001) at an operational level — not as an auditor, but enough to understand why evidence integrity matters</li> <li>RPA tooling experience (UiPath, Power Automate) as fallback for portals that defeat headless browsers</li> <li>Prior work in infrastructure operations, data center, or physical security environments</li> <li>Experience building internal tooling or developer-facing portals (not just scripts)</li> </ul> <p></p> <h3 data-path-to-node="0"><strong data-path-to-node="0" data-index-in-node="0">Compensation</strong></h3> <ul data-path-to-node="1

structure</strong></p> <ul> <li>Collaborate with Cloudflare’s Treasury team on the company’s broader capital markets strategy, including debt, convertible, and other structured transactions, and contribute analysis on capital structure, liquidity, and cost of capital.</li> <li>Develop and maintain a credible network of financing counterparties — banks, private credit funds, private equity, lessors, infrastructure investors, and OEM/vendor finance teams.</li> <li>Monitor market conditions, pricing, and emerging financing structures, and bring new ideas to leadership.</li> </ul> management of financing arrangements, including covenant compliance, reporting obligations, and ongoing counterparty relationships.</li> <li>Use AI-native tooling and automation to scale the function — models, trackers, and workflows that let a small team operate with speed and accuracy.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Examples of desirable skills, knowledge and experience</strong></p> <ul> <li><strong>10+ years of experience</strong> across structured or project finance, infrastructure investing, private credit, equipment leasing, private equity, investment banking, and/or corporate capital markets — ideally including time in-house at a high-growth technology or infrastructure company.</li> <li><strong>A track record of leading complex financing transactions through to close</strong>, including direct negotiation and documentation with external counterparties.</li> <li><strong>The ability to run a financing workstream independently</strong>, without close supervision, and to represent the company credibly with senior external counterparties.</li> <li><strong>Deep structuring expertise</strong> — e.g., equipment finance, leasing and sale-leaseback, asset-backed and project finance, vendor financing, and debt or convertible capital markets — plus creativity in designing new structures to meet company goals.</li> <li><strong>Advanced financial modeling, credit analysis, and transaction documentation skills</strong>, including familiarity with credit agreements, master lease agreements, and related legal documentation.</li> <li><strong>Working knowledge of the accounting and tax implications</strong> of financing structures, and comfort partnering with Accounting, Tax, and Legal to get them right.</li> <li><strong>Exceptional written and verbal communication skills</strong>, with the ability to make complex structures legible to non-specialist leadership and to influence diverse stakeholders.</li> <li><strong>Comfort with ambiguity</strong> — the ability to drive clarity, manage competing priorities, and execute at a high bar in a fast-moving environment.</li> <li><strong>High-trust collaboration</strong> — the ability to build credibility quickly with senior internal stakeholders (CFO, Treasury, Legal, Accounting, Infrastructure) and external counterparties.</li> <li><strong>AI-native curiosity and skill</strong> — fluency with modern AI tooling and a track record of using it to amplify your impact.</li> <li><strong>Sound judgment with confidential information</strong>, including an understanding of the discretion required at a public company.</li> <li><strong>Sector background</strong> in data centers, digital infrastructure, telecom, cloud, or AI compute preferred; existing relationships with lenders, lessors, and infrastructure investors a plus.</li> <li>MBA, CFA, or similar a plus, but not required.</li> </ul> <p> </p> <p><strong>Compensation</strong></p> <p>Compensation may be adjusted depending on work location.</p> <ul> Internet properties powered by Cloudflare all have web traffic routed through its intelligent global network, which gets smarter with every request. As a result, they see significant improvement in performance and a decrease in spam and other attacks. Cloudflare was named to Entrepreneur Magazine’s Top Company Cultures list and ranked among the World’s Most Innovative Companies by Fast Company.</p> <p>At Cloudflare, we’re not looking for people who wait for a polished roadmap; we’re looking for the builders who see the cracks in the Internet that everyone else has simply learned to live with. We value candidates who have the instinct to spot a "normalized" problem and the AI-native curiosity to create a solution using the latest tools. Our culture is built on iteration, leveraging AI to ship faster today to make it better tomorrow, while ensuring that every improvement, no matter how small, is shared across the team to lift everyone up. If you’re the type of person who values curiosity over bureaucracy, and that AI is a partner in solving tough problems to keep the Internet moving forward, you’ll fit right in.</p></div><h3>Hiring Locations: <strong>Atlanta, GA, Austin, US, New York, NY, San Francisco, CA, Seattle, WA, Washington DC, US</strong></h3> <h3>About the Department</h3> <p>Infrastructure Operations builds and manages the data center infrastructure behind Cloudflare's global network. The organization brings together engineering, operations, hardware and logistics teams that plan, deploy, operate and maintain our footprint in hundreds of cities worldwide. In this role, you'll help extend that footprint with a new generation of data center sites across the United States.</p> <h3>About the Role</h3> <p>We're looking for an experienced Data Center Operations manager to build and run the team that brings these new sites online and keeps them running around the clock.</p> <p>You will build a distributed team of Data Center Engineers from the ground up. You'll own sites across their full lifecycle: delivering greenfield builds through third-party vendors and colocation partners, running them in production, and retiring hardware securely at end of life. You'll be accountable for production hardware availability, 24x7 on-site response, and the operating model that lets this footprint scale.</p> <p>The role means balancing competing demands every day: build deadlines against build quality, dependence on partners against high standards, and fast incident response against careful compliance. You need to keep both sides of each in view.</p> <p>This role covers the physical layer: hardware, cabling, and Layer 1/Layer 2 connectivity. It works closely with network engineering and server provisioning teams but does not own them.</p> <h3>What You'll Do</h3> <p>Team Leadership</p> <ul> <li> <p>Hire, develop and manage Data Center Engineers based on-site at data centers across the US. Set clear expectations, career paths and a culture of ownership across a team spread over many sites.</p> </li> <li> <p>Build and take part in a 24x7 on-call rotation with your team. Define coverage models, handover protocols and incident SLAs that hold up as the footprint grows.</p> </li> <li> <p>Serve as the escalation point for on-site incidents. Coordinate engineers, colocation providers and vendors to restore service quickly, and lead root-cause analysis after major incidents so the same problem doesn't happen again.</p> </li> </ul> <p>Site Delivery</p> <ul> <li> <p>Own build timelines from site readiness through hardware delivery, rack-and-stack, cabling, validation and handoff to production.</p> </li> <li> <p>Run greenfield builds as multi-workstream programs. Coordinate third-party integrators, contractors and colocation providers to hit dates without cutting corners.</p> </li> <li> <p>Be on-site during key build phases to oversee vendor work, verify quality and make sure sites are production-ready.</p> </li> </ul> <p>Production Operations</p> <ul> <li> <p>Be accountable for availability targets for production hardware at your sites. Run break/fix, repairs, RMAs and spares strategy so that availability is measured, reported and improving.</p> </li> <li> <p>Manage colocation providers and vendors day to day: escalations, remote-hands quality, power and cooling issues, and performance against contractual commitments.</p> </li> </ul> <p>Documentation and DCIM</p> <ul> <li> <p>Make sure every site is fully documented in DCIM from day one. That covers rack elevations, power and cabling, asset location, and lifecycle status, all recorded as hardware arrives rather than filled in later.</p> </li> <li> <p>Treat infrastructure records as a source of truth that both operations and dependent teams rely on, giving them accurate, current visibility into where hardware is and what state it's in.</p> </li> <li> <p>Partner with tooling teams to bring DCIM online at new sites, and define documentation standards that hold up as the footprint grows.</p> </li> </ul> <p>Decommissioning and Hardware Lifecycle</p> <ul> <li> <p>Own on-site decommissioning end to end: unracking, physical collections, serial number verification, chain of custody, and handoff for secure destruction.</p> </li> <li> <p>Partner with vendor management on IT asset disposition (ITAD) vendors. Make sure destruction certificates and compliance evidence are filed and audit-ready.</p> </li> </ul> <p>Security and Compliance</p> <ul> <li> <p>Make sure your sites and team meet Cloudflare's physical security, access control, chain-of-custody and compliance obligations.</p> </li> <li> <p>Follow established physical access procedures, and work with security and compliance teams to develop new ones where these sites need them.</p> </li> <li> <p>Support audits with accurate, timely evidence. Treat audit readiness as a continuous standard, not something you prepare for once per audit cycle.</p> </li> </ul> <p>Automation and Operational Efficiency</p> <ul> <li> <p>Find manual, repetitive work in build, break/fix, decommissioning and evidence collection. Influence tooling and automation teams to remove it.</p> </li> <li> <p>Evaluate and adopt AI-assisted workflows for incident triage, root-cause analysis, documentation and compliance evidence generation.</p> </li> <li> <p>Scale the operation through tooling, not just headcount.</p> </li> </ul> <p>Business Reporting</p> <ul> <li> <p>Own weekly business reviews and monthly and quarterly reporting on availability, build progress, incidents and operational health to the Director and peer leaders.</p> </li> <li> <p>Partner with network, systems, hardware, supply chain and infrastructure engineering teams to make sure physical operations support what runs on top of them.</p> </li> </ul> <h3>Who You Are</h3> <p><strong>A builder who stays to operate.</strong> You've stood up sites and teams, and you take ownership of what happens after go-live. Delivering a build is where your job starts. If it isn't documented, it isn't done.</p> <p><strong>A leader of distributed teams.</strong> You've hired and built trust with on-site engineers spread across many locations, most of whom you won't see day to day. You know how to create accountability, consistent standards and a shared culture across sites, both remotely and in person.</p> <p><strong>Firm with partners.</strong> You hold colocation providers and vendors to high standards without becoming adversarial. You know the contract, you track performance, and you escalate when it's warranted.</p> <p><strong>Compliance-minded without being a compliance specialist.</strong> You understand why access controls and decommissioning chain of custody are audit controls. You treat compliance as part of doing the work well, not as overhead.</p> <p><strong>Automation-first.</strong> When something hurts, your first instinct is to fix the process or the tooling, not add people. You can turn an operational pain point into requirements engineering teams can act on.</p> <h3>Required Experience</h3> <ul> <li> <p>6+ years in data center operations, including 3+ years directly managing on-site technical teams. This role is a great fit for you if:</p> <ul> <li>You have led and developed a high-performing engineering team(s) and can point to what that team shipped and how the people on it grew.</li> <li>You are technically credible with experienced blockchain and systems engineers.
